body.en: Advanced geometry on the EST II includes angle theorems, triangle congruence and similarity, and properties of quadrilaterals and regular polygons.

Parallel lines cut by a transversal: alternate interior angles are equal; co-interior (same-side) angles are supplementary. Triangle congruence: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS. Similarity: AA, SAS, SSS — corresponding sides proportional. Exterior angle = sum of two non-adjacent interior angles.

In triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle A = 48°\) and \(\angle B = 63°\). Find the exterior angle at \(C\).

Exterior angle \(= \angle A + \angle B = 48° + 63° = 111°\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Triangles, Polygons & Area

body.en:
• Linear vs. Area vs. Volume Scale Factors: If two similar polygons have a linear scale factor of \(k\), their perimeters scale by \(k\), but their areas scale by \(k^2\). On EST II, questions often provide the ratio of areas (e.g. \(9:16\)) and ask for perimeter — take the square root (\(3:4\)) first!
  • Regular Polygon Angle Inversions: Interior angle is \(\frac{(n-2)180°}{n}\), while exterior angle is \(\frac{360°}{n}\). Notice that \(\text{interior} + \text{exterior} = 180°\). It is almost always faster to compute the exterior angle first and subtract from \(180°\).
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: For any valid triangle with sides \(a, b, c\), the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third: \(a + b > c\), \(a + c > b\), \(b + c > a\). This implies \(|a - b| < c < a + b\).
  • Heron's Formula vs. Trigonometric Area: If all 3 sides are known, use Heron's formula: \(A = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where semi-perimeter \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\). If two sides and included angle are known, use \(\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\).

question.en: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm with an included angle of 90°. Find the hypotenuse and all angles.
A regular hexagon has side length \(s = 6\) cm. (a) Calculate the exact area of the hexagon. (b) Find the length of the long diagonal connecting two opposite vertices.

solution.en:
(a) Exact area: A regular hexagon is composed of 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length \(s = 6\). The area of one equilateral triangle is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(36) = 9\sqrt{3}\). Total area is: \[ A = 6 \times 9\sqrt{3} = 54\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2 \approx 93.53\text{ cm}^2. \]

(b) Long diagonal: The long diagonal passes through the center of the circumscribed circle and equals twice the side length: \(d = 2s = 2(6) = 12\text{ cm}\).
